domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and potential cancellation. References the employee, the leave type/policy, and the actor who performed each state-changing action.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — initial state; employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers; can be edited freely
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted for manager review; visible to the employee's manager; no longer editable by the employee
APPROVED — manager has approved the request; leave balance is decremented; employee can still cancel which triggers balance restoration
REJECTED — manager has rejected the request; terminal state (no further transitions); balance is unaffected
CANCELLED — request was withdrawn; can transition from DRAFT (employee discards), SUBMITTED (employee withdraws before decision), or APPROVED (employee cancels after approval; balance is restored)

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behavior. Each leave type (annual, sick, emergency) maps to one active policy at a time.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; can be referenced by new leave requests and balance calculations
INACTIVE — policy has been disabled; existing balances referencing it remain valid but new requests cannot use it
ARCHIVED — policy is retired; historical reference only; no new balances or requests can reference it

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved (increment usedDays) or cancelled after approval (decrement usedDays).
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect; can be consumed by approved leave requests
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays is zero; no further leave of this type can be approved until more days are accrued or the next fiscal year
FROZEN — balance is temporarily locked (e.g., during payroll processing or investigation); no deductions or accruals allowed

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. The employee is the actor who applies for leave and the subject whose balances are tracked. The managerId field establishes the approval hierarchy — a leave request is routed to the employee's manager for approval.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — employee is currently employed and eligible for leave
INACTIVE — employee is on extended leave or suspension; leave requests may be restricted
TERMINATED — employment has ended; no new leave requests allowed; historical balances preserved

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Represents a notification triggered by leave lifecycle events. Sent to employees (e.g., approval/rejection notices) and managers (e.g., new requests awaiting action). Each notification is linked to the originating leave request for traceability.
lifecycle_states: PENDING — notification has been created but not yet delivered
SENT — notification has been delivered to the recipient
READ — recipient has acknowledged/read the notification
ARCHIVED — notification is no longer shown in the active feed

business_rules: BR-001 — Leave Request Date Validation: startDate must be on or before endDate. A leave request cannot span zero or negative days. The calculated duration in working days must be >= 1.

BR-002 — No Retrospective Leave: startDate must be on or after the current date at the time of submission (not creation in DRAFT). Emergency leave is exempt from this rule — it may be submitted up to 3 calendar days after the start date.

BR-003 — Minimum Notice Period: For annual leave, the startDate must be at least `minimumNoticeDays` (from LeavePolicy) after the submission date. Sick and emergency leave are exempt from the minimum notice requirement.

BR-004 — Sufficient Balance Check: At approval time, the employee's LeaveBalance.remainingDays for the corresponding policy must be >= the requested number of working days. If remainingDays is insufficient, the request must be rejected. The check is performed at approval time, not submission time.

BR-005 — Balance Deduction on Approval: When a leave request transitions from SUBMITTED to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the working-day duration of the leave, and remainingDays is recalculated. This operation must be atomic.

BR-006 — Balance Restoration on Cancellation: When an APPROVED leave request transitions to CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by the working-day duration of the leave, and remainingDays is recalculated. This operation must be atomic.

BR-008 — No Overlapping Approved Leave: An employee cannot have two APPROVED leave requests whose date ranges overlap. The overlap check considers all APPROVED requests for the same employee regardless of leave type. SUBMITTED requests that overlap with an APPROVED request should be flagged but are not automatically rejected — the manager decides.

BR-007 — Manager Authorization: Only the employee's designated manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a SUBMITTED leave request. A manager cannot approve or reject their own leave requests. If an employee has no manager (managerId is null), the request is auto-escalated to the department head or HR.

BR-009 — Active Employee Only: Only employees with employmentStatus = 'ACTIVE' may submit leave requests. Employees with status 'INACTIVE' or 'TERMINATED' are blocked from creating or submitting new requests. Existing APPROVED requests for a terminated employee remain valid through their end date.

BR-010 — Active Policy Only: A leave request can only reference a LeavePolicy with isActive = true. If a policy is deactivated (INACTIVE or ARCHIVED), new requests cannot be created against it, but existing requests in any state remain valid.

BR-012 — Emergency Leave Constraints: Emergency leave requests are limited to a maximum of 5 working days per request. An employee may not submit more than 3 emergency leave requests per fiscal year. These limits are validated at submission time.
